title: How QR Codes Survive Damage

aiSpeech.voice_selection: User-selected narration voice; one continuous take; no alternate voice used
aiSpeech.tempo_algorithm: FFmpeg atempo WSOLA; pitch preserved; never faster than source
aiSpeech.alignment: faster-whisper medium.en word timestamps on exact paced narration master
aiSpeech.asr_tail_filter: Excluded 0 ASR tokens beginning in digital silence at or after 41.736646s
aiSpeech.asr_spurious_token_filter: Excluded 0 ASR tokens lasting <=0.10s with probability <0.20; exact full-script match still required

vo.text: This code stores the word HELLO.
vo.speak: This code stores the word HELLO.

vo.text: Scan it, and the reader rebuilds HELLO.

vo.text: Now cover some of these central squares.

vo.text: A QR code stores extra error-correction information alongside the message.
vo.speak: A QR code stores extra error-correction information alongside the message.

vo.text: Watch the reader use that information to work out what the missing values should be.
vo.speak: Watch the reader use that information to work out what the missing values should be.

vo.text: The reader fills in those missing values, and HELLO is recovered.

vo.text: The large corner patterns have another job: helping the reader find and align the code.

vo.text: Cover too much data, and the reader no longer has enough information to rebuild the message.

vo.text: Error correction gives the reader a second chance to recover the message.
